messages:
Ethan (Partnerships): Quick sync 1 - SI wants to embed our private-offer credits into their managed-deployment package. Need clarity on how credits apply across marketplace metered listings vs. marketplace reserved SKUs.
Priya (SI): Buyer story: they buy SI-managed bundle (hardware + services) and get an offer code that reduces cloud consumption for first 6 months. We prefer credits visible in checkout to avoid manual invoicing.
Jonah (MarketplaceOps): Visible credits are fine for metered listings. For reserved SKUs we don't allow front-line discounts to exceed seat-level pricing without a PO. We can show a 'Partner Credit' line but reserved will require rebate flow.
Mei (Legal): Important: credits must be explicitly one-time and non-renewing. Also need language to prevent credits being used to meet minimum committed spend.
Anya (RevenueOps): If SI wants credits to count toward committed thresholds (to trigger capacity discounts) we need finance sign-off. That could create accounting distortion. Prefer credits not count toward committed usage.
Priya (SI): Understood. Can we compromise: credits apply to net-billed consumption but are excluded from committed-baseline calculations? Buyer experience still sees lower first invoices.
Ethan (Partnerships): That could work. Actionable asks: 1) Jonah confirm UI text for 'Partner Credit' during checkout 2) Mei provide PO appendix clause 3) Anya define committed-spend exclusion verbiage 4) Priya confirm SI's customer-facing FAQ.
Jonah (MarketplaceOps): Draft UI text: "Partner Credit (applies at checkout). Credit applies to metered usage only; reserved capacity rebates handled post-sale." Will add to the marketplace copy repo.
Mei (Legal): PO appendix draft snippet: "Migration/Partner Credits are one-time, non-recurring, and do not contribute to committed-spend baselines or renewal pricing unless explicitly stated in a separate written agreement."
Anya (RevenueOps): Will draft an explanatory note for ARR recognition and renewals: credits reduce cash collected but do not reduce committed ARR floor. I'll put an example calculation in the sheet.
Priya (SI): Two practical asks from SI: a) co-sell listing on marketplace homepage during launch week b) 30-day payment window for appliance invoice. Both tied to commit of $X over 12 months.
Ethan (Partnerships): Co-sell placement is doable if we meet partner marketing SLAs. Payment terms need finance ok. Linking sheet: https://tinyurl.com/si-appliance-coop. Please add the requested commit amount and marketing assets.
marketplace-bot: Reminder: Promotions/placements must be approved by MarketplaceOps 14 days before launch.
Jonah (MarketplaceOps): Note: homepage placements require a certified listing and approved creative. PID for campaign: MPC-2026-SI1.
Mei (Legal): Also flagging IP joint announcement checklist. Need approvals from both legal teams before any PR.
Anya (RevenueOps): Can we set a cap on total credit exposure per customer? Ops prefers a per-customer cap (e.g., $150k) to limit runway risk.
Priya (SI): Cap is fine, but SI asks for a clause to escalate exceptions for strategic deals.
Ethan (Partnerships): We'll add a waiver path: Partnerships + RevenueOps sign-off for strategic exceptions. Tracking sheet updated.
Jonah (MarketplaceOps): Action items updated in the sheet. I'll push UI copy and campaign PID by EOD tomorrow.
Priya (SI): We'll draft the customer FAQ and add use-cases.
Mei (Legal): I'll circulate the PO appendix + joint-PR checklist to internal and SI legal for comment.
Anya (RevenueOps): I'll publish the ARR example and the cap rule.
Ethan (Partnerships): Great. Tentative timeline: finalize terms by next Wed, marketplace assets complete by Fri, soft announcement the following week if all green. :spiral_calendar_pad: 
Priya (SI): thanks all.
Ethan (Partnerships): Closing loop after legal review.
